text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Police force defends its wide use of telephone bugging. Says it has solved many cases of political violence.
- Main opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz made a call for toppling Islamist-led government and replacing it with a broad-based one.
- Members of True Path Party junior coalition partner in row over whether to withdraw from government.
- Police give out chocolates at Istanbul University in public relations exercise for "police week".
- German parliamentary delegation will attend the second anniversary of protests for those who "disappeared" in police custody.
- Governors of 80 provinces are called to Ankara to discuss how to implement the decisions by a military-dominated board to fight against Islamist activism.
- Some 22,000 oil workers on work go-slow because no wage agreement has been reached.
- The directorate general of religious affairs opens web site on the internet.
